title: Voyage of the Scarlet Queen
paragraphs: A serialized seafaring adventure following Captain Philip Karney, first mate Gallagher, and the crew of the Scarlet Queen through dangerous ports and Pacific intrigue.

Serialized high-seas adventure built around the ketch Scarlet Queen, Captain Philip Karney and first mate Red Gallagher. The frozen GRH snapshot preserves the audition plus 33 of the 35 regular broadcasts; regular episodes #7 and #10 are missing.
GRH documents the program through Mutual sustaining regular run (July 3, 1947 to February 25, 1948) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Elliott Lewis (performer on 34 recordings), Edwin Max (performer on 33 recordings), Richard Aurandt (music on 29 recordings, performer on 2 recordings, composer on 1 recording, and conductor on 1 recording), Charles Arlington (announcer on 30 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Gil Doud (writer on 30 recordings), Robert Tallman (writer on 28 recordings and radio adaptor on 1 recording), and James Burton (producer on 13 recordings and director on 3 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.87e6f64937f0bfb8|KHJ]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include maritime and high-seas adventure, continuing voyage and port-to-port travel, shipboard crew life and command, Pacific and Asian port settings, crime, theft and intrigue, and cargo, merchants and port commerce.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar Pacific adventure radio, Mutual sustaining adventure programming, Maritime sound design and location realism, and 1940s American radio portrayals of Pacific and Asian locales.
